menu-title.purpose: Pause, guide and settings headings, Bold.

region-speaker.purpose: Map region and dialogue speaker, Bold.

level-title.purpose: Lesson header, Bold; journey uses the shorter task role.

journey-task.purpose: Journey gameplay destination and map task, Bold.

body.purpose: Feedback, instruction, help and result copy, Regular.

focus.purpose: Selected symbol in optional precision controls, Regular.

secondary.purpose: Map restored count, Regular; Skip story uses Bold at this size.

receiver-label.purpose: Complete destination label, Bold; compensated by canvas scale.

device.purpose: Explanation text, Regular, compensated by canvas scale; device glyphs use Bold.

token-glyph.purpose: Live Bold face that lifts and scales with the held token.

target-glyph.purpose: Live Bold face in the complete receiver order.

shadows.name: soft-contact
shadows.purpose: Native contact shader on fitted quads beneath tokens, platforms and receiver; references colors.contact-shadow. Playing pieces seat their mesh bottom on visible wood at 0.365 of the padded floor rectangle; token shadows align just below that surface. Cast Unity shadows are disabled.

motion.name: hold-preview
motion.purpose: Native body and live glyph scale/lift together while fixed cells retain hit testing. X displacement is bounded to 1.15 cell spacings, or 3.15 with a Ribbon Reach charge; upward pointer delta to 0.45 cell spacings.

motion.name: selection
motion.purpose: Focus selection, distinct from immediate held feedback. Reduced Motion applies focus directly.

motion.name: exchange
motion.purpose: Short opposing arcs describe the committed atomic adjacent, linked or charged endpoint exchange.

motion.name: device-response
motion.purpose: Local rail recoil capped at 0.025 world units. Screen shake is opt-in, off by default, and suppressed by Reduced Motion.

motion.name: fall-and-land
motion.value: 300ms quadratic vertical fall + at least 240ms damped two-stage landing
motion.purpose: Map source pieces to committed destinations. Landing uses abs(sin(t * 2pi)) * exp(-3t) * 0.13 world-unit lift; damped alternating rotation up to 5deg and up to 8% squash. Reduced Motion has no bounce. Presentation only.

motion.name: delivery
motion.purpose: Result UI follows final visual synchronization. Dust/audio tails do not determine gameplay or command completion.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: No causal travel, recoil or deformation; at most two stationary dust fades per burst. Ambient layers show phase zero.

motion.name: ambient-wheel
motion.purpose: Legacy wheel phase remains in source, but the incidental lower-right wheel is hidden in the current surface.

motion.name: ambient-clouds
motion.value: normalized phase rates 0.017 / 0.026 / 0.035 per second; wrap span 1.7
motion.purpose: Three separate transparent cloud planes at different depths and widths; original art tinted by region.

motion.name: ambient-plants
motion.purpose: Mirrored lower-corner cutouts pivot about their stems; side offset is 0 or 1.

motion.name: ambient-glider
motion.value: angle = phase * 0.07; x = sin(angle) * viewportWidth * 0.34; rotation = -6deg + sin(angle) * 9deg
motion.purpose: Whole rotated 3:2 image fits the bounded gap between feedback and top floor. Height is at most min(viewportHeight * 0.05, gap * 0.5), vertical drift is gap * 0.08. Hidden during held input or unavailable gap; menu pose is separate.

motion.name: ambient-lifecycle
motion.value: unscaled presentation phase; stop while paused or suspended
motion.purpose: Presentation-only. Explicit pause and suspension stop phase; map/dialogue decoration can continue while puzzle input is paused. Reduced Motion paints phase zero.

motion.name: wood-load-and-wind
motion.value: target sag 0.045 world units × grounded weight; wind sin(phase × 0.65 + floor × 0.52) × 0.025
motion.purpose: Bounded springs bend the painted strip and sway two continuous hemp ropes from above the viewport through rail attachments to the receiver. Holding releases apparent weight; deterministic puzzle state remains authoritative.

motion.name: pictorial-guide
motion.value: 7s demonstration loop; Reduced Motion fixed at 2s
motion.purpose: Source-piece cause/effect over precomputed resolver outcomes. Reduced Motion shows stationary before ghosts and settled after pose; no playable commands.

motion.name: regional-weather
motion.value: native separate rain/snow/pollen meshes and map UI; presentation-clock phase
motion.purpose: Eight original regional backgrounds; live layer movement follows explicit pause/suspension and Reduced Motion. No gameplay-state authority.

breakpoints.name: precision-input
breakpoints.value: explicit Comfort preference; no width or row-count breakpoint

breakpoints.name: supported-orientation
breakpoints.value: portrait enforced on iOS/Android; 1440 × 900 desktop-wide baseline; 844 × 390 landscape diagnostic rejected; short desktop windows unsupported

lighting.name: workshop-key-and-fill
lighting.value: warm directional key: intensity 1.05, RGB (1, 0.96, 0.88); sky fill: intensity 0.35, RGB (0.64, 0.85, 1); flat ambient RGB (0.69, 0.79, 0.80)
lighting.purpose: Native Unity scene illumination, no cast shadows; existing surface tokens unchanged.

components.name: Descend / Deliver and travel
components.description: Native Unity Button with gold nine-slice Image, Bold TMP and ColorBlock tints. Gameplay height is compensated; menu/dialogue heights follow their native layout. Descend becomes Deliver only at a matching final-floor row. Documentation is native-only; HTML/CSS preview intentionally absent.

components.name: Utility and menu action
components.description: Native warm paper Button. Gameplay actions are compensated 48-unit bands; the button-menu variant uses 60 reference units. Custom keyboard focus treatment is not established. Documentation is native-only; HTML/CSS preview intentionally absent.

components.name: Optional precision control
components.description: Native authored chevron focus controls and left/right exchange actions. Enabled explicitly in Comfort; never forced by row length. Documentation is native-only; HTML/CSS preview intentionally absent.

components.name: Held persistent piece
components.description: Native beveled symbol mesh plus live TMP glyph. Immediate lift, 1.10–2.5 scale toward a 64-pixel face, fixed input cells and adjacent legality preview, plus one charged endpoint exchange across one/two intervening pieces in R01–R06. Body and glyph move together; release routes through the existing resolver. Documentation is native-only; HTML/CSS preview intentionally absent.

components.name: Regional platform
components.description: Native compact WoodBoard strip with body-band UV framing, continuous braided hemp suspension through rail attachments to the receiver, brass hardware, strength pips and graphite seams. platform backgroundColor is only the missing-texture fallback; the shipped surface is painted raster grain. Reuses stable SymbolId contact faces. Source-piece falls, bounded springs and wood chips consume committed events. Native-only; HTML/CSS preview intentionally absent.

components.name: Complete receiving cradle
components.description: Native gold rim, ivory inset, sockets and the complete ordered target. Inspectable through target zoom; fail compares target and delivered row, win seats the row before result actions. Documentation is native-only; HTML/CSS preview intentionally absent.

components.name: Journey route and stop
components.description: Native uGUI over eight original regional art kits and 33 pages for 160 nodes. Usually five plaza-aligned stops; four on final pages of new 24-node regions. Mika marks the actual current stop; saved stamp goals derive map seals. Separate clouds and rain/snow move on the presentation clock. Native-only; HTML/CSS preview intentionally absent.

components.name: Story frame
components.description: Native paper nine-slice panel, thin brass detail, live speaker and short dialogue with Continue/Skip story. Original alpha portrait and regional background. Opening dialogue pauses puzzle input. Documentation is native-only; HTML/CSS preview intentionally absent.

components.name: Comfort and sound setting
components.description: Native labelled paper row with track color and positional knob. Preferences persist in the checksum-protected local schema1 profile. Larger text excludes symbol faces and explicit font/layout overrides remain. Documentation is native-only; HTML/CSS preview intentionally absent.

components.name: Exact-order magnifier
components.description: Native safe-area paper surface with four columns and up to two rows, original shape contours/live glyphs and position labels. Pauses gameplay; no browser counterpart. Documentation is native-only; HTML/CSS preview intentionally absent.

narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "The Sky Wind Workshop"**

A small keeper carries light through floating islands and wind-powered toy machines. Painted honey wood, braided hemp, warm brass, ivory letter tiles and six colored silhouettes make the puzzle tangible. Mika's patched overalls, saffron scarf and lantern connect the mechanism to a warm, imperfect character. Painted regional skies and isometric routes give each delivery a place and a neighbour.

Real beveled meshes, an orthographic view, live lettering and separate illustrated scenery share the same bright storybook world. The hand touches the row directly; quiet controls leave room for the machine and its complete gold destination. Paper panels support short dialogue and navigation. This is the author-delegated, code-led extension of the established world; no approved composite image exists for pixel-perfect fidelity claims.

This record merges the implemented P14 journey revision into the P12/P13 system. Sources are `CascadeGame.cs`, `.Flow.cs`, `.Journey.cs`, `.Touch.cs`, `TokenSlot.cs`, `ToyMachineView.cs`, `LayeredWorld.cs`, `JourneyStory.cs`, `ToyAssetBuilder.cs` and `MotionProfile.asset`. `Docs/JOURNEY_SURFACE_BRIEF.md` owns the surface contract; `Docs/P14_FLOW.md` owns implementation scope and validation limits. Native captures and review live in `Reports/Journey`. `Docs/JOURNEY_ASSET_PROVENANCE.md` records the 12 original regional/character rasters; earlier mesh, font and audio provenance remains in the P12/P13 documents. The sidecar records native components and motion, with no fabricated HTML/CSS counterparts. Its synthesized tonal ramps are preview aids, not shipped palette additions.

P16 extends these existing controls with durable local progress and recovery in `CascadeGame.Save.cs`, `Persistence/` and `Application/AttemptRecord.cs`. `Docs/P16_SAVE.md` owns the save contract; `Reports/P16` holds native recovery fixtures and test evidence. This extension adds no visual tokens or raster assets. Editor evidence does not verify physical-device power loss, OS kill, full player builds, native-language approval or human enjoyment.

P17 extends the same paper, mint and brass surfaces with a travel bag, journal,
requests, workshop, keepsake collection, earned parcel and personal routes in
`CascadeGame.Rewards.cs`. `JourneyRewards.cs`, `PlayerProfile.cs` and
`CascadeGame.Save.cs` supply the local facts behind those views;
`Docs/P17_META.md` owns their progression contract. Nine new transparent
illustrations keep the incumbent painted material character; exact prompts and
alpha/margin limitations are in `Docs/META_ASSET_PROVENANCE.md`. This ordinary
extension adds no shared visual tokens. `Reports/P17/README.md` records 333/333
EditMode, 46/47 full PlayMode and a corrected focused 1/1 navigation result,
plus 44 inspected native frames, including three requested carousel views. The
independent verdict scores both listed findings resolved, disposition ship at P17 scope. The approved wooden workshop extension now follows the contracts in
`Docs/VISUAL_MOTION_REWORK.md` and `Docs/WOODLAND_SURFACE_BRIEF.md`.

P18 makes two narrow clarity corrections within this world: the stable `Hint`
key displays `Помощь`/`Поміч` in RU/UK, and map paging reuses the authored
direction chevron. `Docs/P18_INTEGRATION.md` owns this phase's contract;
`Reports/P18/impeccable-review.md` records ship at this correction scope. Three
final 320 × 693 native Editor frames confirm the corrected RU caption, RU guide
and UK map against the existing system. The 3/3 focused tests and matching
157-puzzle traces establish their stated behavior boundaries; the roughly
100 ms whole-Editor frame observation is not a device performance pass.
Physical devices, final player build, child comprehension and human enjoyment
remain unverified. This historical phase added no visual tokens or artwork. The current wood,
motion and world extension is recorded below.

The Woodland checkpoint uses `ToyMachineView.Woodland.cs`, `PuzzleEventPlayer.cs`,
`CascadeGame.DeviceDemo.cs`, `WoodBoardGraphic.cs`, `WorldMotion.cs`,
`WorldWeatherGraphic.cs`, `LayeredWorld.cs` and the expanded `JourneyStory.cs`.
Eight regional art kits now cover 160 stops over 33 pages; three original kits
are retained and five original Base/Map pairs plus WoodBoard are documented in
`Docs/WOODLAND_ASSET_PROVENANCE.md`. Source-piece trajectories and board springs
are presentation effects over the unchanged deterministic rule core. Native
stills and sampled motion live in `Reports/Woodland`; the 5/5 EditMode and
16/16 focused PlayMode checkpoint predates the final guide/CanvasRenderer fix.
The final renderer correction passed 4/4 affected UI regressions in
`Reports/WoodlandFix/playmode.xml` at 11:29:09–11:29:16 UTC; fresh native guide,
map and bag captures show wood/weather. Review/build were pending at that
historical checkpoint; the Craft results below supersede those statuses. Physical iOS/Android, haptics, mobile performance,
non-reader understanding, native editorial, live Ads/IAP and human enjoyment
remain NOT RUN. The service boundary is disabled mock code; online remains
design-only. These Woodland results are historical checkpoints.

The Craft extension follows `Docs/CRAFT_REWORK.md`: `CascadeGame.Craft.cs`,
`CascadeGame.Rewards.cs`, `ToyMachineView.Ropes.cs`, `ToyMachineView.Woodland.cs`,
`PuzzleEventPlayer.cs` and `LayeredWorld.cs` implement object shelves, simultaneous
selection, continuous ropes, visual weight and composed scenery. Six optional
R01–R06 Ribbon Reach trials now use the shared deterministic resolver under
rules2.1-longreach; C01–C160 retain rules2.0 and their content hashes. The original
WorkshopRoom and WindGardenPanorama generated rasters and metadata are recorded
in `Docs/AssetPrompts/Craft/provenance.json`, with exact prompts alongside them.
The palette, font, symbols and paper/wood/brass identity are preserved.
`Reports/Craft/design-documentation.md` records source evidence and remaining
validation limits. `Reports/Craft/impeccable-verdict.md` records ship for seven
scored findings, including map edges and physical grounding; it does not approve
the entire product. `Reports/CraftFinal/playmode.xml` passed three affected
regressions, a subset of the earlier seven. The Mac standalone build succeeded
with zero errors and 346 warnings. A locked-Mac C160 player sample at 1440 × 900
on M4 Pro measured median 16.703 ms / p95 17.520 ms over 240 frames after 90
warm-up frames. The invalid GC counter supplies no allocation evidence. This
short sample is neither verified foreground nor mobile performance. Native
player visual confirmation is blocked by the locked Mac; physical devices,
human enjoyment and release readiness remain unverified.
keyCharacteristics: Direct touch lifts a piece and its live glyph together; the receiver stays visible.
Six stable silhouettes and colors retain their identity across eight regions.
Wood grain, hemp suspension, brass joints and soft contact shadows make the machine tangible.
Mika, Pip and Rue connect short optional dialogue to a concrete destination.
Illustrated routes distinguish the current path from future-region browsing.
Separate clouds, rooted plants, a glider and regional weather give the sky restrained life.

rules.name: The Shared Identity Rule
rules.body: Use the same silhouette and material for a SymbolId in the row, target, device contact and magnifier; glyph symbols use live text on ivory bodies.

rules.name: The Live Face Rule
rules.body: Move and scale a letter with its mesh face through selection, holding, exchange and landing; never bake gameplay letters into scenery.

rules.name: The Complete Machine Rule
rules.body: Keep the persistent row, remaining floors and complete receiver order visible together; changing row length must preserve clear physical rail proportions.

rules.name: The Honest Path Rule
rules.body: Distinguish the browsed stop from the reached stop; future art must never imply unlocked or saved progress.

rules.name: The Clear Flight Rule
rules.body: Decorative motion must fit wholly outside the row, receiver and feedback; a lower render layer alone is not sufficient separation.

dos: **Do** reuse each authored silhouette and material wherever its SymbolId appears.
**Do** move and scale the live glyph with its selected or held body.
**Do** preserve the complete target and the direct-touch default.
**Do** keep precision controls an explicit Comfort preference.
**Do** bind the map marker to saved first-clear campaign receipts and label future previews honestly.
**Do** select the story's region before showing its character and dialogue.
**Do** bound ambient art outside gameplay information and freeze its phase while paused or suspended.
**Do** inspect native 390 × 844, 320 × 693 and wide Editor captures after layout changes.
**Do** preserve original assets, licenses, generation provenance and Unity meta identities.
donts: **Don't** turn physical rails into full-width rectangular cards or restore the crowded default toolbar.
**Don't** bake gameplay text into imagery or change symbol identity to indicate state.
**Don't** let presentation, animation completion, scenery, physics or ad callbacks change puzzle state.
**Don't** portray browsed islands as reached or unsaved previews as durable progress.
**Don't** describe online concepts or disabled mock Ads/IAP boundaries as live integration; Ribbon Reach is local optional play, not a purchased ability.
**Don't** describe local ranks, known parcels or keepsakes as global online services; their saved local implementations are documented in PRODUCT.md.
**Don't** copy ShapeMania screens, characters, sprites, props or materials into this world.
**Don't** equate Editor captures and automated tests with device, haptic, performance, build, native-language or human-enjoyment proof.
